<h1 id="goldelox-internal-functions">GOLDELOX Internal Functions</h1>
<div class="pdf-hide">
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The older format of the internal functions manual is included in Workshop4 installation and can be found under:</p>
<p><em>C:\Users\Public\Documents\4D Labs\4DUpdates\Manuals</em></p>
<p>You can also download this document below:</p>
<p><a class="md-button" href="https://4dsystems.com.au/downloads/Software/4D-Workshop4-IDE/documents/GOLDELOX_internalfunctions_R_7_3.pdf">Download <span class="twemoji"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512"><!--! <h2 id="introduction">Introduction</h2>
<p>The 4D Labs family of embedded graphics processors are powered by a highly optimised soft core virtual engine, E.V.E. (Extensible Virtual Engine).</p>
<p>EVE is a proprietary, high performance virtual processor with an extensive byte-code instruction set optimised to execute compiled 4DGL programs. 4DGL (4D Graphics Language) was specifically developed from ground up for the EVE engine core. It is a high-level language which is easy to learn and simple to understand yet powerful enough to tackle many embedded graphics applications.</p>
<p><img alt="GOLDELOX-GFX2 Internal Block Diagram" class="pdf-hide" src="../img/goldelox/image3.png"></p>
<p>4DGL is a graphics-oriented language allowing rapid application development. An extensive library of graphics, text and file system functions and the ease of use of a language that combines the best elements and syntax structure of languages such as C, Basic, Pascal, etc. Programmers familiar with these languages will feel right at home with 4DGL. It includes familiar instructions such as <code>IF..ELSE..ENDIF, WHILE..WEND, REPEAT..UNTIL, GOSUB..ENDSUB, GOTO</code> and a wealth of (chip-resident) internal functions that include <code>SERIN, SEROUT, GFX_LINE, GFX_CIRCLE</code> and many more.</p>
<p>This document covers the internal (chip-resident) functions available for the GOLDELOX Processor. This document should be used in conjunction with the <a href="../">4DGL Programmers Reference Manual</a>.</p>
<p>GOLDELOX Internal functions can be categorized based on usage as listed below:</p>
<p><img alt="GOLDELOX-GFX2 Internal Block Diagram" class="float-right pdf-only width-60" src="../img/goldelox/image3.png"></p>
<ul>
<li><a href="#gpio-functions">GPIO</a></li>
<li><a href="#memory-access-functions">Memory Access</a></li>
<li><a href="#user-stack-functions">User Stack</a></li>
<li><a href="#math-functions">Math</a></li>
<li><a href="#text-and-string-functions">Text and String</a></li>
<li><a href="#graphics-functions">Graphics</a></li>
<li><a href="#display-io-functions">Display I/O</a></li>
<li><a href="#media-sdsdhc-card-or-serial-flash-chip-functions">Media (SD/SDHC or Serial Flash)</a></li>
<li><a href="#flash-memory-chip-functions">Flash Memory Chip</a></li>
<li><a href="#spi-control-functions">SPI Control</a></li>
<li><a href="#serial-uart-communication-functions">Serial (UART) Communication</a></li>
<li><a href="#sound-and-tune-rtttl-functions">Sound and Tune (RTTTL)</a></li>
<li><a href="#general-purpose-functions">General Purpose</a></li>
</ul>
<h2 class="page-break" id="gpio-functions">GPIO Functions</h2>
<h3 id="pin_set">pin_Set</h3>
<p>GOLDELOX-GFX2 has limited but powerful I/O.</p>
<p>There are pre-defined constant for <strong>mode</strong> and <strong>pin</strong>:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Pin Constant</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO1</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO2</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>The following are the supported modes for the pins:</p>

<h3 id="joystick">joystick</h3>
<p>Returns the value of the Joystick position (5 position switch implementation).
The JOYSTICK values are:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: center;">5</th>

<a id="__codelineno-4-3" name="__codelineno-4-3" href="#__codelineno-4-3"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">joy</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">==</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"UP   "</span><span class="p">);</span>

</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The joystick input uses IO1 utilizing the A/D converter. Each switch is connected to junction of 2 resistors that form a unique voltage divider circuit. Refer to the GOLDELOX-GFX2 data sheet example schematics for the required resistor values.</p>

<a id="__codelineno-8-24" name="__codelineno-8-24" href="#__codelineno-8-24"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"result="</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OW_Reset</span><span class="p">());</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-25" name="__codelineno-8-25" href="#__codelineno-8-25"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">OW_Write</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mh">0xEE</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// start conversion</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-26" name="__codelineno-8-26" href="#__codelineno-8-26"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">OW_Reset</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// reset</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-27" name="__codelineno-8-27" href="#__codelineno-8-27"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">OW_Write</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mh">0xAA</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// get temperature</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-28" name="__codelineno-8-28" href="#__codelineno-8-28"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="nl">temp_buf</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OW_Read</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-29" name="__codelineno-8-29" href="#__codelineno-8-29"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">OW_Reset</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// optional</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-30" name="__codelineno-8-30" href="#__codelineno-8-30"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">OW_Write</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xAC</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// optional read status</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-31" name="__codelineno-8-31" href="#__codelineno-8-31"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="nl">stat_buf</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OW_Read</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// optional 82 when DS1821 run</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-32" name="__codelineno-8-32" href="#__codelineno-8-32"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">txt_MoveCursor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-33" name="__codelineno-8-33" href="#__codelineno-8-33"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"temp_buf=0x"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">HEX2</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">temp_buf</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-34" name="__codelineno-8-34" href="#__codelineno-8-34"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">txt_MoveCursor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-35" name="__codelineno-8-35" href="#__codelineno-8-35"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"stat_buf=0x"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">HEX2</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">stat_buf</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-8-36" name="__codelineno-8-36" href="#__codelineno-8-36"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">forever</span>

</code></pre></div>
<h2 id="memory-access-functions">Memory Access Functions</h2>
<h3 id="peekb">peekB</h3>
<p>This function returns the 8 bit value that is stored at <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>peekB(address);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Address</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The address of a memory byte. The address is usually a pre-defined <a href="../#8-bit-registers-memory-map">system register address constant</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The 8 bit value stored at <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-9-1" name="__codelineno-9-1" href="#__codelineno-9-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example places the width of the display</span>
<a id="__codelineno-9-2" name="__codelineno-9-2" href="#__codelineno-9-2"></a><span class="c1">// (horizontal resolution in pixel units) in 'myvar'</span>
<a id="__codelineno-9-3" name="__codelineno-9-3" href="#__codelineno-9-3"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-9-4" name="__codelineno-9-4" href="#__codelineno-9-4"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">peekB</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">GFX_XMAX</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">+</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The <a href="#peekb">peekB(..)</a> and <a href="#pokeb">pokeB(..)</a> functions are usually only used with internal system byte registers using the pre-defined constants. If <a href="#peekb">peekB(..)</a> or <a href="#pokeb">pokeB(..)</a> are used to access other locations, the address must be doubled to get the correct pointer address.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="peekw">peekW</h3>
<p>This function returns the 16 bit value that is stored at <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   peekW(address);</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">address</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The address of a memory word. The address is usually a pre-defined <a href="../#16-bit-registers-memory-map">system register address constant</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The 16 bit value stored at <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-10-1" name="__codelineno-10-1" href="#__codelineno-10-1"></a><span class="cm">/*</span>
<a id="__codelineno-10-2" name="__codelineno-10-2" href="#__codelineno-10-2"></a><span class="cm"> * This example places the low word of the 32 bit system timer in 'myvar'.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-10-3" name="__codelineno-10-3" href="#__codelineno-10-3"></a><span class="cm"> * The equivalent operation using a pointer is: myvar := *TIMER2;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-10-4" name="__codelineno-10-4" href="#__codelineno-10-4"></a><span class="cm"> */</span>
<a id="__codelineno-10-5" name="__codelineno-10-5" href="#__codelineno-10-5"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-10-6" name="__codelineno-10-6" href="#__codelineno-10-6"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">peekW</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SYSTEM_TIMER_LO</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="pokeb">pokeB</h3>
<p>This function writes a 8 bit value to a location specified by <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>pokeB(address, byte_value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">address</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The address of a memory byte. The address is usually a pre-defined <a href="../#8-bit-registers-memory-map">system register address constant</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">byte_value</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The lower 8 bits of <strong>byte_value</strong> will be stored at <strong>address</strong>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: If poke address was a legal address (usually ignored).                   </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-11-1" name="__codelineno-11-1" href="#__codelineno-11-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example manually adjusts the top clipping point to 10 pixels down from top of screen.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-11-2" name="__codelineno-11-2" href="#__codelineno-11-2"></a><span class="n">pokeB</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">CLIP_TOP</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The <a href="#peekb">peekB(..)</a> and <a href="#pokeb">pokeB(..)</a> functions are usually only used with internal system byte registers using the pre-defined constants. If <a href="#peekb">peekB(..)</a> or <a href="#pokeb">pokeB(..)</a> are used to access other locations, the address must be doubled to get the correct pointer address.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="pokew">pokeW</h3>
<p>This function writes a 16 bit value to a location specified by <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>pokeW(address, word_value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">address</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The address of a memory word. The address is usually a pre-defined <a href="../#16-bit-registers-memory-map">system register address constant</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">word_value</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The 16 bit word_value will be stored at <strong>address</strong>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  If poke address was a legal address (usually ignored).                                   </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-12-1" name="__codelineno-12-1" href="#__codelineno-12-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example sets TIMER2 to 5 seconds.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-12-2" name="__codelineno-12-2" href="#__codelineno-12-2"></a><span class="n">pokeW</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">TIMER2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5000</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-12-3" name="__codelineno-12-3" href="#__codelineno-12-3"></a><span class="c1">// The equivalent operation using a pointer is:</span>
<a id="__codelineno-12-4" name="__codelineno-12-4" href="#__codelineno-12-4"></a><span class="c1">//*TIMER2 := 5000;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="bits_set">bits_Set</h3>
<p>This function sets the required bits at address by 'ORing' the mask with the value stored at <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bits_Set(address, mask);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">address</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The address of a user memory location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mask</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The 16 bit mask containing bits to be set.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-13-1" name="__codelineno-13-1" href="#__codelineno-13-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example sets bits 6 and 7 of myval</span>
<a id="__codelineno-13-2" name="__codelineno-13-2" href="#__codelineno-13-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-13-3" name="__codelineno-13-3" href="#__codelineno-13-3"></a><span class="nl">myval</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-13-4" name="__codelineno-13-4" href="#__codelineno-13-4"></a><span class="n">bits_Set</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xC0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-13-5" name="__codelineno-13-5" href="#__codelineno-13-5"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">HEX</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The bits_Set, bits_Clear, bits_Flip and bits_Test functions can only be used for user memory and will not work with system register variables</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="bits_clear">bits_Clear</h3>
<p>This function clears the required bits at address by 'ANDing' the inverted mask with the value stored at <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bits_Clear(address, mask);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">address</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The address of a user memory location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mask</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The 16 bit mask containing bits to be cleared.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-14-1" name="__codelineno-14-1" href="#__codelineno-14-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example clears bits 10, 11, 12 and 13 of myval</span>
<a id="__codelineno-14-2" name="__codelineno-14-2" href="#__codelineno-14-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-14-3" name="__codelineno-14-3" href="#__codelineno-14-3"></a><span class="nl">myval</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xFFFF</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-14-4" name="__codelineno-14-4" href="#__codelineno-14-4"></a><span class="n">bits_Clear</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x3C00</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-14-5" name="__codelineno-14-5" href="#__codelineno-14-5"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">HEX</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The bits_Set, bits_Clear, bits_Flip and bits_Test functions can only be used for user memory and will not work with system register variables.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="bits_flip">bits_Flip</h3>
<p>This function flips the required bits at address by 'XORing' the mask with the value stored at <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bits_Flip(address, mask);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">address</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The address of a user memory location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mask</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The 16 bit mask containing bits to be flipped.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-15-1" name="__codelineno-15-1" href="#__codelineno-15-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example clears bits 15, 11, and 1 of myval</span>
<a id="__codelineno-15-2" name="__codelineno-15-2" href="#__codelineno-15-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-15-3" name="__codelineno-15-3" href="#__codelineno-15-3"></a><span class="nl">myval</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xFFFF</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-15-4" name="__codelineno-15-4" href="#__codelineno-15-4"></a><span class="n">bits_Flip</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x8802</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-15-5" name="__codelineno-15-5" href="#__codelineno-15-5"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">HEX</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The bits_Set, bits_Clear, bits_Flip and bits_Test functions can only be used for user memory and will not work with system register variables.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="bits_test">bits_Test</h3>
<p>This function tests the required bits at <strong>address</strong> using the mask with the original value. If any of the bits are set, the function returns 1. If none of the bits are set, the function returns 0.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bits_Test(address, mask);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">address</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The address of a user memory location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mask</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">The 16 bit mask containing bits to be tested.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Results</em></strong>: if any of the tested bits are set returns 1. If none of the tested bits are set return 0.                           </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-16-1" name="__codelineno-16-1" href="#__codelineno-16-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example tests bits 8-15 in myval, if any bits are set, the result will be 1.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-16-2" name="__codelineno-16-2" href="#__codelineno-16-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-16-3" name="__codelineno-16-3" href="#__codelineno-16-3"></a><span class="n">myval</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x1234</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-16-4" name="__codelineno-16-4" href="#__codelineno-16-4"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">bits_Test</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myval</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xFF00</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-16-5" name="__codelineno-16-5" href="#__codelineno-16-5"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">res</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The bits_Set, bits_Clear, bits_Flip and bits_Test functions can only be used for user memory and will not work with system register variables.</p>
</div>
<h2 class="page-break" id="user-stack-functions">User Stack Functions</h2>
<p>EVE provides all the requirement for a user stack to aid in development of stack-based processing (e.g., for interpreters and fast raster drawings).
The stack is at a fixed location (it is at the base of the user memory). The stack pointer always expects the stack to be here – it is hard micro-coded internally.</p>
<p>If none of the stack functions are used, the stack can be disregarded as it will not influence any other program dynamics – the memory can be used for other purposes.
If a user stack is required, it must be configured as the first array in the user's program. The stack pointer always points to the current item on top of the stack. </p>
<p>Typically, your program will look like this:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-17-1" name="__codelineno-17-1" href="#__codelineno-17-1"></a><span class="c1">// the user stack MUST be the first storage in you program</span>
<a id="__codelineno-17-2" name="__codelineno-17-2" href="#__codelineno-17-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mystack</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w">            </span><span class="c1">// A 20 word stack. The stack must be the first array in the program. </span>
<a id="__codelineno-17-3" name="__codelineno-17-3" href="#__codelineno-17-3"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar2</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// etc</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If the stack pointer is zero, there are no items on the stack.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="setsp">setsp</h3>
<p>The users stack pointer is zeroed at power up, but it is sometimes necessary to alter the stack pointer for various reasons, such as running multiple concurrent stacks, or resetting to a known position as part of an error recovery process.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>setsp(index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">This argument is used to set the users SP to the required position. The stack pointer is set to zero during power-up initialisation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-18-1" name="__codelineno-18-1" href="#__codelineno-18-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example sets the users stack pointer to 'empty'</span>
<a id="__codelineno-18-2" name="__codelineno-18-2" href="#__codelineno-18-2"></a><span class="n">setsp</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// reset the stack pointer</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="getsp">getsp</h3>
<p>This function returns the current stack index into the stack array. If the index is zero, there are no items on the stack.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntx</em></strong>:   <code>getsp();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The current stack index.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-19-1" name="__codelineno-19-1" href="#__codelineno-19-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print '1' assuming there are no other items on the stack.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-19-2" name="__codelineno-19-2" href="#__codelineno-19-2"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1234</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-19-3" name="__codelineno-19-3" href="#__codelineno-19-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">getsp</span><span class="p">());</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// print the stack index</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="pop">pop</h3>
<p>This function returns the value at the current stack pointer index. The stack pointer is then decremented, so it now points to the item below. If the stack pointer is zero, (ie a pop was performed on an empty stack) the function returns 0 and the stack pointer is not altered (ie it remains at 0).</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>pop();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value at current stack pointer index.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-20-1" name="__codelineno-20-1" href="#__codelineno-20-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example prints '300' and the stack pointer is reduced by 2</span>
<a id="__codelineno-20-2" name="__codelineno-20-2" href="#__codelineno-20-2"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-20-3" name="__codelineno-20-3" href="#__codelineno-20-3"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-20-4" name="__codelineno-20-4" href="#__codelineno-20-4"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">pop</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="o">+</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">pop</span><span class="p">());</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="push">push</h3>
<p>Increment the user stack pointer first and then places the item into the user stack array at the current position. The stack pointer is now pointing to this new item.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>push(value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Argument to be pushed to the user stack.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-21-1" name="__codelineno-21-1" href="#__codelineno-21-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example pushes 3 items to the user stack</span>
<a id="__codelineno-21-2" name="__codelineno-21-2" href="#__codelineno-21-2"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-21-3" name="__codelineno-21-3" href="#__codelineno-21-3"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1234</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-21-4" name="__codelineno-21-4" href="#__codelineno-21-4"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">5678</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-21-5" name="__codelineno-21-5" href="#__codelineno-21-5"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="drop">drop</h3>
<p>Decrements the user stack pointer determined by the value <strong>n</strong>. If n exceeds the stack index, the stack pointer is zeroed.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>drop(n);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">n</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of items to be dropped from the stack.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-22-1" name="__codelineno-22-1" href="#__codelineno-22-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example decrements the stack pointer by 2, effectively dropping</span>
<a id="__codelineno-22-2" name="__codelineno-22-2" href="#__codelineno-22-2"></a><span class="c1">// 'myvar' and '5678' from the stack, the next pop would yield 1234.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-22-3" name="__codelineno-22-3" href="#__codelineno-22-3"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-22-4" name="__codelineno-22-4" href="#__codelineno-22-4"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1234</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-22-5" name="__codelineno-22-5" href="#__codelineno-22-5"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">5678</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-22-6" name="__codelineno-22-6" href="#__codelineno-22-6"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-22-7" name="__codelineno-22-7" href="#__codelineno-22-7"></a><span class="n">drop</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="call">call</h3>
<p>Calls the specified function, the arguments to the called function are from the stack. The stacked parameters are consumed and the stack pointer is altered to match the number of arguments that were consumed.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>call();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  If the called function returns a value then it is available.                  |</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-23-1" name="__codelineno-23-1" href="#__codelineno-23-1"></a><span class="c1">// takes the function argument count, function pointer, and argument pointer</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-2" name="__codelineno-23-2" href="#__codelineno-23-2"></a><span class="c1">// from the top of the stack and calls the function using the stacked parameters.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-3" name="__codelineno-23-3" href="#__codelineno-23-3"></a><span class="c1">// The 7 arguments on the stack are discarded.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-4" name="__codelineno-23-4" href="#__codelineno-23-4"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-5" name="__codelineno-23-5" href="#__codelineno-23-5"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-6" name="__codelineno-23-6" href="#__codelineno-23-6"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-7" name="__codelineno-23-7" href="#__codelineno-23-7"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-8" name="__codelineno-23-8" href="#__codelineno-23-8"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mh">0xFFFF</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-9" name="__codelineno-23-9" href="#__codelineno-23-9"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">gfx_RectangleFilled</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// push the function call address</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-10" name="__codelineno-23-10" href="#__codelineno-23-10"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                   </span><span class="c1">// push the argument count</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-11" name="__codelineno-23-11" href="#__codelineno-23-11"></a><span class="c1">//~~~~~~</span>
<a id="__codelineno-23-12" name="__codelineno-23-12" href="#__codelineno-23-12"></a><span class="n">call</span><span class="p">();</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="exec">exec</h3>
<p>Calls the specified function, passing the arguments to the called function from the stack. The stack and stack pointer are not altered.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>::   <code>exec(functionPtr, argCount);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">functionPtr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A pointer to a function which will utilise the stacked arguments.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">argCount</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The count of arguments on the stack that are to be passed to the function call.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  If the called function returns a value then it is available.  </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-24-1" name="__codelineno-24-1" href="#__codelineno-24-1"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="c1">// set some arbitrary values on the stack</span>

<a id="__codelineno-24-3" name="__codelineno-24-3" href="#__codelineno-24-3"></a><span class="n">push</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">);</span>

<a id="__codelineno-24-5" name="__codelineno-24-5" href="#__codelineno-24-5"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-24-6" name="__codelineno-24-6" href="#__codelineno-24-6"></a><span class="c1">// Draws a circle using the stacked parameters.</span>

<a id="__codelineno-24-9" name="__codelineno-24-9" href="#__codelineno-24-9"></a><span class="w">                    </span><span class="c1">// the stacked parameters</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="sin">SIN</h3>
<p>This function returns the sine of an <strong>angle</strong>. The input value is automatically shifted to lie within 0-359 degrees.</p>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>SIN(angle);</code></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="rand">RAND</h3>
<p>This function returns a pseudo random signed number ranging from -32768 to +32767.</p>
<p>Returns a pseudo random signed number ranging from -32768 to +32767 each time the function is called. The random number generator may first be seeded by using the SEED(number) function. The seed will generate a pseudo random sequence that is repeatable. You can use the modulo operator (%) to return a number within a certain range, eg n := RAND() % 100; will return a random number between -99 and +99. If you are using random number generation for random graphics points, or only require a positive number set, you will need to use the ABS function so only a positive number is returned, eg: X1 := ABS(RAND() % 100); will set co-ordinate X1 between 0 and 99. Note that if the random number generator is not seeded, the first number returned after reset or power up will be zero. This is normal behavior. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>RAND();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: pseudo random signed number ranging from -32768 to +32767</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-31-1" name="__codelineno-31-1" href="#__codelineno-31-1"></a><span class="n">SEED</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1234</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-31-2" name="__codelineno-31-2" href="#__codelineno-31-2"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print '3558, 1960' to the display.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-31-3" name="__codelineno-31-3" href="#__codelineno-31-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="s">", "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">());</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="seed">SEED</h3>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>SEED(number);</code></p>

</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<a id="__codelineno-32-2" name="__codelineno-32-2" href="#__codelineno-32-2"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print '30129, 27266' to the display.</span>

<h3 id="ovf">OVF</h3>
<p>This function returns the high order 16 bits from certain math and shift functions. It is extremely useful for calculating 32 bit address offsets for MEDIA access.
It can be used with the shift operations, addition, subtraction, multiplication and modulus operations.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>OVF();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The high order 16 bits from certain math and shift functions. </p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="text-and-string-functions">Text and String Functions</h2>
<h3 id="txt_movecursor">txt_MoveCursor</h3>
<p>Moves the origin to a screen position set by line and column parameters. The line and column position is calculated, based on the size and scaling factor for the currently selected font. When text is outputted to screen it will be displayed from this position. The text position could also be set with <a href="#gfx_moveto">gfx_MoveTo(...)</a>; if required to set the text position to an exact pixel location. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>txt_MoveCursor(line, column);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">line</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Holds a positive value for the required line position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">column</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Holds a positive value for the required column position.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-35-1" name="__codelineno-35-1" href="#__codelineno-35-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example moves the text origin to the 5th line and the 10th column.</span>

</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="putstr">putstr</h3>
<p>This function prints a string to the current output stream, usually the display. The argument can be a string constant, a pointer to a string, a pointer to an array, or a pointer to a data statement. This is more efficient than <a href="#print">print(...)</a> function</p>
<ul>
<li>A string constant is automatically terminated with a zero.</li>
<li>A string in a data statement is not automatically terminated with a zero.</li>
<li>All variables in 4DGL are 16-bit, if an array is used for holding 8-bit characters, each element stores 2 characters.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>putstr(pointer);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pointer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A string constant or word pointer to a string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Returns the pointer to the item that was printed.         </p>

<a id="__codelineno-41-2" name="__codelineno-41-2" href="#__codelineno-41-2"></a><span class="nl">v</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mo">0567</span><span class="mi">8</span><span class="p">;</span>

<a id="__codelineno-41-4" name="__codelineno-41-4" href="#__codelineno-41-4"></a><span class="n">putnum</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BIN</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="c1">// print the number as binary 16 digits</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="print">print</h3>
<p>This function provides a verstaitle way to format numerics and strings to a formatted text. It can accept directives passed in square brackets to make it print in various ways.</p>
<p>For instance, if you wish to print a number in 4 digit hex, use the <code>[HEX4]</code> directive placed in front of the variable to be displayed within the print statement. Refer to <a href="#num_print_formats">List of Predefined Signed Decimal Formats</a> for all the numeric representations available</p>
<p><code>[STR]</code> and <code>[CHR]</code> are additional directives that are not part of the numeric set.</p>
<ul>
<li>The <code>[STR]</code> directive expects a string pointer to follow.</li>
<li>The <code>[CHR]</code> directive prints the character value of a variable.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>print(...);</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="tabbed-set tabbed-alternate" data-tabs="2:3" style="--md-indicator-x: 16px; --md-indicator-width: 71px;"><input checked="checked" id="__tabbed_2_1" name="__tabbed_2" type="radio"><input id="__tabbed_2_2" name="__tabbed_2" type="radio"><input id="__tabbed_2_3" name="__tabbed_2" type="radio"><div class="tabbed-labels"><label for="__tabbed_2_1">Simple</label><label for="__tabbed_2_2">Mixed</label><label for="__tabbed_2_3">Print Modes</label></div>
<div class="tabbed-content">
<div class="tabbed-block">
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-42-1" name="__codelineno-42-1" href="#__codelineno-42-1"></a><span class="c1">// In it's simplest form, print will simply print a number as can be seen below:</span>
<a id="__codelineno-42-2" name="__codelineno-42-2" href="#__codelineno-42-2"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-42-3" name="__codelineno-42-3" href="#__codelineno-42-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
</div>
<div class="tabbed-block">
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-43-1" name="__codelineno-43-1" href="#__codelineno-43-1"></a><span class="c1">// print 100 to the current output device (usually the display in TEXT mode).</span>
<a id="__codelineno-43-2" name="__codelineno-43-2" href="#__codelineno-43-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-43-3" name="__codelineno-43-3" href="#__codelineno-43-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"the value of myvar is :- "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"and its 8bit binary representation is:-"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">BIN8</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-43-4" name="__codelineno-43-4" href="#__codelineno-43-4"></a><span class="c1">// Note:   if you wish to add a string anywhere within a print(...) statement,</span>
<a id="__codelineno-43-5" name="__codelineno-43-5" href="#__codelineno-43-5"></a><span class="c1">//         just place a quoted string expression and you will be able to mix strings</span>
<a id="__codelineno-43-6" name="__codelineno-43-6" href="#__codelineno-43-6"></a><span class="c1">//         and numbers in a variety of formats.</span>
</code></pre></div>
</div>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>You can freely mix string pointers, strings, variables and expressions within a print statement. <strong>print(...)</strong> can also use the <a href="#to"><strong>to(...)</strong></a> function to redirect it's output to a different output device other than the screen using the function (refer to the <a href="#to"><strong>to(...)</strong></a> statement for further examples).</p>
</div>
<h3 id="to">to</h3>
<p>This function can be to to redirect the printouts that are normally printed on the screen.</p>
<p>Normally, print just sends its output to the display in <strong>TEXT</strong> mode which is the default, however, the output from print can be sent to <strong>COM0</strong>, and <strong>MDA</strong> (media) 'streams'. This function can also stream to a memory array to compose and store a string for later use.</p>
<p>Note that once the <strong>to(...)</strong> function has taken effect, the stream reverts back to the default stream which is <strong>TEXT</strong> as soon as <strong>putch</strong>, <strong>putstr</strong>, <strong>putnum</strong> or <strong>print</strong> has completed its action.</p>
<p>The <strong>APPEND</strong> argument is used to send the printed output to the same place as the previous redirection. This is most useful for building string arrays, or adding sequential data to a media stream.</p>
<p>The following are accepted outstream constants</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Predefined Name</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Constant</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Redirection</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><strong>APPEND</strong></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the same stream that was previously assigned. Output is appended to user array if previous redirection was to an array.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><strong>COM0</strong></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0xFF04</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirected to the <strong>COM</strong> (serial) port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><strong>TEXT</strong></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0xFF08</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>screen</strong> (default).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><strong>MDA</strong></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0xFF10</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>SD/SDHC</strong> or <strong>FLASH</strong> media.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>Alternaltively, a pointer (0x102 &lt; 0x3FF) to a buffer/array can be used as outstream. In this case, the printouts is redirected to the memory location.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>to(outstream);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">outstream</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A variable or constant specifying the destination for the <strong>putch</strong>, <strong>putstr</strong>, <strong>putnum</strong> and <strong>print</strong> functions.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-45-1" name="__codelineno-45-1" href="#__codelineno-45-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// a buffer that will hold up to 20 bytes/chars</span>
<a id="__codelineno-45-2" name="__codelineno-45-2" href="#__codelineno-45-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">               </span><span class="c1">// a var for use as a pointer</span>

<a id="__codelineno-45-4" name="__codelineno-45-4" href="#__codelineno-45-4"></a><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"ONE "</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// redirect putstr to the buffer</span>

<a id="__codelineno-45-6" name="__codelineno-45-6" href="#__codelineno-45-6"></a><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">APPEND</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"THREE</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="charwidth">charwidth</h3>
<p><strong>charwidth</strong> is used to calculate the width in pixel units for a character, based on the currently selected font. The font can be proportional or mono-spaced. If the total width of the string exceeds 255 pixel units, the function will return the 'wrapped' (modulo 8) value.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>charwidth('char');</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">'char'</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The ascii character for the width calculation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The width of a single character in pixel units.   </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-46-1" name="__codelineno-46-1" href="#__codelineno-46-1"></a><span class="nl">str</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"HELLO</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">THERE"</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// note that this string spans 2 lines due</span>

<a id="__codelineno-46-3" name="__codelineno-46-3" href="#__codelineno-46-3"></a><span class="nl">width</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">strwidth</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">str</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// get the width of the string, this will</span>
<a id="__codelineno-46-4" name="__codelineno-46-4" href="#__codelineno-46-4"></a><span class="w">                        </span><span class="c1">// also capture the</span>
<a id="__codelineno-46-5" name="__codelineno-46-5" href="#__codelineno-46-5"></a><span class="nl">height</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">strheight</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// note, invoking strwidth also calcs height</span>
<a id="__codelineno-46-6" name="__codelineno-46-6" href="#__codelineno-46-6"></a><span class="w">                        </span><span class="c1">// which we can now</span>
<a id="__codelineno-46-7" name="__codelineno-46-7" href="#__codelineno-46-7"></a><span class="c1">// The string above spans 2 lines, strheight() will calculate height</span>
<a id="__codelineno-46-8" name="__codelineno-46-8" href="#__codelineno-46-8"></a><span class="c1">// correctly for multiple lines.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-46-9" name="__codelineno-46-9" href="#__codelineno-46-9"></a><span class="nl">len</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">strlen</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">str</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// the strlen() function returns the number</span>

<h3 id="charheight">charheight</h3>
<p><strong>charheight(char)</strong> is used to calculate the height in pixel units for a character, based on the currently selected font. The font can be proportional or mono-spaced.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>charheight('char');</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">'char'</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The ascii character for the height calculation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The height of a single character in pixel units.  </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth()</a></p>
<h3 id="strwidth">strwidth</h3>
<p><strong>strwidth()</strong> returns the width of a zero terminated string in pixel units. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strwidth(pointer);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pointer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The pointer to a zero (0x00) terminated string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The width of a string in pixel units. </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth()</a></p>
<h3 id="strheight">strheight</h3>
<p><strong>strheight()</strong> returns the height of a zero terminated string in pixel units. The <a href="#strwidth"><strong>strwidth()</strong></a> function must be called first which makes available width and height. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strheight();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The height of a string in pixel units.    </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth()</a></p>
<h3 id="strlen">strlen</h3>
<p><strong>strlen()</strong> returns the length of a zero terminated string in character units. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strlen(pointer);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pointer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The pointer to a zero (0x00) terminated string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The length of a string in character units.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth()</a></p>
<h3 id="txt_set">txt_Set</h3>
<p>Given a function number and a value, set the required text control parameter, such as size, colour, and other formatting controls. This function is extremely useful in a loop to select multiple parameters from a data statement or a control array. Note also that each function available for txt_Set has a single parameter 'shortcut' function that has the same effect.
(see the <strong>Single parameter short-cuts for the txt_Set functions</strong> next page)</p>

<h3 id="gfx_cls">gfx_Cls</h3>
<p>Clear the screen using the current background colour</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Cls();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-47-1" name="__codelineno-47-1" href="#__codelineno-47-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example clears the entire display using colour DARKGRAY</span>
<a id="__codelineno-47-2" name="__codelineno-47-2" href="#__codelineno-47-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_BGcolour</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DARKGRAY</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-47-3" name="__codelineno-47-3" href="#__codelineno-47-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="gfx_changecolour">gfx_ChangeColour</h3>
<p>Changes all <strong>oldColour pixels</strong> to <strong>newColour</strong> within the clipping area.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_ChangeColour(oldColour, newColour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">oldColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the sample colour to be changed within the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">newClour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the new colour to change all occurrences of old colour within the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-48-1" name="__codelineno-48-1" href="#__codelineno-48-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example prints a test string, forces the clipping area to the extent</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-2" name="__codelineno-48-2" href="#__codelineno-48-2"></a><span class="c1">// of the text that was printed, then changes the background colour.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-3" name="__codelineno-48-3" href="#__codelineno-48-3"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-4" name="__codelineno-48-4" href="#__codelineno-48-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">txt_Width</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-5" name="__codelineno-48-5" href="#__codelineno-48-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">txt_Height</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-6" name="__codelineno-48-6" href="#__codelineno-48-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">8</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-7" name="__codelineno-48-7" href="#__codelineno-48-7"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"TEST"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// print the string</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-8" name="__codelineno-48-8" href="#__codelineno-48-8"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">gfx_SetClipRegion</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// force clipping area to extents of text</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-9" name="__codelineno-48-9" href="#__codelineno-48-9"></a><span class="w">                        </span><span class="c1">// just printed.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-10" name="__codelineno-48-10" href="#__codelineno-48-10"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">gfx_ChangeColour</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BLACK</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RED</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// test change of background colour</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-11" name="__codelineno-48-11" href="#__codelineno-48-11"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">repeat</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">forever</span>
<a id="__codelineno-48-12" name="__codelineno-48-12" href="#__codelineno-48-12"></a><span class="n">endfunc</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_circle">gfx_Circle</h3>
<p>Draws a circle with centre point x1, y1 with radius r using the specified colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Circle(x, y, radius, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the center of the circle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">rad</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the radius of the circle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the colour of the circle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-49-1" name="__codelineno-49-1" href="#__codelineno-49-1"></a><span class="c1">// assuming PEN_SIZE is OUTLINE</span>
<a id="__codelineno-49-2" name="__codelineno-49-2" href="#__codelineno-49-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Circle</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x001F</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-49-3" name="__codelineno-49-3" href="#__codelineno-49-3"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a BLUE circle outline centred</span>
<a id="__codelineno-49-4" name="__codelineno-49-4" href="#__codelineno-49-4"></a><span class="c1">// at x=50, y=50 with a radius of 30 pixel units.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The default <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, however, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>SOLID</strong>, the circle will be drawn filled, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, the circle will be drawn as an outline. If the circle is drawn as SOLID, the outline colour can be specified with <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_OutlineColour(...)</strong></a>. If <strong>OUTLINE_COLOUR</strong> is set to 0, no outline is drawn.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_circlefilled">gfx_CircleFilled</h3>
<p>Draws a <strong>SOLID</strong> circle with centre point x1, y1 with radius using the specified colour.
The outline colour can be specified with <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_OutlineColour(...)</strong></a>. If <strong>OUTLINE_COLOUR</strong> is set to 0, no outline is drawn.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_CircleFilled(x, y, rad, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the center of the circle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">rad</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the radius of the circle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the colour of the circle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><em>Example</em></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-50-1" name="__codelineno-50-1" href="#__codelineno-50-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a filled RED circle with a YELLOW outline</span>
<a id="__codelineno-50-2" name="__codelineno-50-2" href="#__codelineno-50-2"></a><span class="c1">// at x=25, y=25 with a radius of 10 pixel units.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-50-3" name="__codelineno-50-3" href="#__codelineno-50-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_OutlineColour</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mh">0xFFE0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-50-4" name="__codelineno-50-4" href="#__codelineno-50-4"></a><span class="n">gfx_CircleFilled</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">25</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">25</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xF800</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>

<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is ignored, the circle is always drawn <strong>SOLID</strong>.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_line">gfx_Line</h3>
<p>Draws a line from x1,y1 to x2,y2 using the specified colour. The line is drawn using the current object colour. The current origin is not altered. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_LinePattern(...)</strong></a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Line(x1, y1, x2, y2, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the starting coordinates of the line.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the ending coordinates of the line.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the line</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-51-1" name="__codelineno-51-1" href="#__codelineno-51-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a RED line from x1=10, y1=10 to x2=100, y2=100</span>
<a id="__codelineno-51-2" name="__codelineno-51-2" href="#__codelineno-51-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Line</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xF800</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
