<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-52-1" name="__codelineno-52-1" href="#__codelineno-52-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a fast RED horizontal line at y=50, from x1=10 to x2=80</span>
<a id="__codelineno-52-2" name="__codelineno-52-2" href="#__codelineno-52-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Hline</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">880</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xF800</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_vline">gfx_Vline</h3>
<p>Draws a fast vertical line from y1 to y2 at horizontal co-ordinate x using colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Vline(x, y1, y2, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal position of the vertical line.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y1, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the vertical end points of the line.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the vertical line.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-53-1" name="__codelineno-53-1" href="#__codelineno-53-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a fast RED vertical line at x=20, from y1=30 to y2=70</span>
<a id="__codelineno-53-2" name="__codelineno-53-2" href="#__codelineno-53-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Vline</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">70</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xF800</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="gfx_rectangle">gfx_Rectangle</h3>
<p>Draws a rectangle from x1, y1 to x2, y2 using the specified colour. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_LinePattern(...)</strong></a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Rectangle(x1, y1, x2, y2, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner of the rectangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the bottom right corner of the rectangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the rectangle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-54-1" name="__codelineno-54-1" href="#__codelineno-54-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a GREEN rectangle from x1=10, y1=10 to x2=30, y2=30</span>
<a id="__codelineno-54-2" name="__codelineno-54-2" href="#__codelineno-54-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Rectangle</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x07E0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// assuming PEN_SIZE is OUTLINE</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The default <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, however, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>SOLID</strong>, the rectangle will be drawn filled, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, the rectangle will be drawn as an outline. If the rectangle is drawn as SOLID, the outline colour can be specified with <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_OutlineColour(...)</strong></a>. If <strong>OUTLINE_COLOUR</strong> is set to 0, no outline is drawn. The outline may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_LinePattern(...)</strong></a> function.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="gfx_rectanglefilled">gfx_RectangleFilled</h3>
<p>Draws a <strong>SOLID</strong> rectangle from x1, y1 to x2, y2 using the specified colour. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_LinePattern(...)</strong></a> function.
The outline colour can be specified with <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_OutlineColour(...)</strong></a>. If <strong>OUTLINE_COLOUR</strong> is set to 0, no outline is drawn. The outline may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_LinePattern(...)</strong></a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_RectangleFilled(x1, y1, x2, y2, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the top left corner of the rectangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the bottom right corner of the rectangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the colour of the rectangle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-55-1" name="__codelineno-55-1" href="#__codelineno-55-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a filled RED rectangle with a YELLOW outline</span>
<a id="__codelineno-55-2" name="__codelineno-55-2" href="#__codelineno-55-2"></a><span class="c1">// from x1=30,y1=30 to x2=80,y2=80</span>
<a id="__codelineno-55-3" name="__codelineno-55-3" href="#__codelineno-55-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_OutlineColour</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mh">0xFFE0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-55-4" name="__codelineno-55-4" href="#__codelineno-55-4"></a><span class="n">gfx_RectangleFilled</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xF800</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is ignored, the rectangle is always drawn <strong>SOLID</strong>.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_polyline">gfx_Polyline</h3>
<p>Plots lines between points specified by a pair of arrays using the specified colour. The lines may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_LinePattern(...)</strong></a> function. gfx_Polyline can be used to create complex raster graphics by loading the arrays from serial input or from MEDIA with very little code requirement.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Polyline(n, vx, vy, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">n</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the number of elements in the x and y arrays specifying the vertices for the polyline.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vx</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the x coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vy</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the y coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the lines</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="gfx_polygon">gfx_Polygon</h3>
<p>Plots lines between points specified by a pair of arrays using the specified colour. The last point is drawn back to the first point, completing the polygon. The lines may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_LinePattern(...)</strong></a> function. gfx_Polygon can be used to create complex raster graphics by loading the arrays from serial input or from MEDIA with very little code requirement.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Polygon(n, vx, vy, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">n</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the number of elements in the x and y arrays specifying the vertices for the polyline.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vx</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the x coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vy</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the y coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the lines</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-57-1" name="__codelineno-57-1" href="#__codelineno-57-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">vx</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">7</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">vy</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">7</span><span class="p">];</span>

<a id="__codelineno-57-4" name="__codelineno-57-4" href="#__codelineno-57-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// This example draws a simple polygon.</span>

<h3 id="gfx_triangle">gfx_Triangle</h3>
<p>Draws a triangle outline between vertices x1,y1 , x2,y2 and x3,y3 using the specified colour. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_LinePattern(...)</strong></a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Triangle(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the first vertices of the triangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the second vertices of the triangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x3, y3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the third vertices of the triangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the triangle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-58-1" name="__codelineno-58-1" href="#__codelineno-58-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a CYAN triangular outline with vertices at 10,10 30,10 20,30</span>
<a id="__codelineno-58-2" name="__codelineno-58-2" href="#__codelineno-58-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Triangle</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mh">0xFFE0</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_bullet">gfx_Bullet</h3>
<p>Draws a circle or 'bullet point' with radius r at at the current origin using the current object colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Bullet(radius);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">radius</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the radius of the bullet.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-60-1" name="__codelineno-60-1" href="#__codelineno-60-1"></a><span class="c1">// assuming PEN_SIZE is TRANSPARENT and OBJECT_COLOUR is WHITE</span>
<a id="__codelineno-60-2" name="__codelineno-60-2" href="#__codelineno-60-2"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a WHITE circle outline at the current origin with a radius of 5 pixels</span>
<a id="__codelineno-60-3" name="__codelineno-60-3" href="#__codelineno-60-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-60-4" name="__codelineno-60-4" href="#__codelineno-60-4"></a><span class="n">gfx_Bullet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The default <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, however, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>SOLID</strong>, the circle will be drawn filled, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to OUTLINE, the circle will be drawn as an outline. If the circle is drawn as <strong>SOLID</strong>, the outline colour can be specified with <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_OutlineColour(...)</strong></a>.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit</h3>
<p>Sets up the internal pointers for the <a href="#gfx_orbit"><strong>gfx_Orbit(..)</strong></a> result variables. The <strong>&amp;x_orb</strong> and <strong>&amp;y_orb</strong> parameters are the addresses of the variables or array elements that are used to store the result from the <a href="#gfx_orbit"><strong>gfx_Orbit(..)</strong></a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_OrbitInit(&amp;x_dest, &amp;y_dest);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;x_dest, &amp;y_dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the addresses of the storage locations for the orbit calculation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-61-2" name="__codelineno-61-2" href="#__codelineno-61-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-61-3" name="__codelineno-61-3" href="#__codelineno-61-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_OrbitInit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">)</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_orbit">gfx_Orbit</h3>
<p>Sets Prior to using this function, the destination address of variables for the calculated coordinates must be set using the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit"><strong>gfx_OrbitInit(..)</strong></a> function. The <a href="#gfx_orbit"><strong>gfx_Orbit(..)</strong></a> function calculates the x, y coordinates of a distant point relative to the current origin, where the only known parameters are the angle and the distance from the current origin. The new coordinates are calculated and then placed in the destination variables that have been previously set with the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit"><strong>gfx_OrbitInit(..)</strong></a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Orbit(angle, distance);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">angle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the angle from the origin to the remote point. The angle is specified in degrees.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">distance</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the distance from the origin to the remote point in pixel units.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-62-1" name="__codelineno-62-1" href="#__codelineno-62-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-2" name="__codelineno-62-2" href="#__codelineno-62-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_OrbitInit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-3" name="__codelineno-62-3" href="#__codelineno-62-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-4" name="__codelineno-62-4" href="#__codelineno-62-4"></a><span class="n">gfx_Bullet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="c1">// mark the start point with a small WHITE circle</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-5" name="__codelineno-62-5" href="#__codelineno-62-5"></a><span class="n">gfx_Orbit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">// calculate a point 50 pixels away from origin at</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-6" name="__codelineno-62-6" href="#__codelineno-62-6"></a><span class="w">                        </span><span class="c1">// 30 degrees</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-7" name="__codelineno-62-7" href="#__codelineno-62-7"></a><span class="n">gfx_CircleFilled</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mh">0xF800</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// mark the target p oint</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-8" name="__codelineno-62-8" href="#__codelineno-62-8"></a><span class="w">                                            </span><span class="c1">// with a RED circle</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Result is stored in the variables that were specified with the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit"><strong>gfx_OrbitInit(..)</strong></a> function.</p>

<h3 id="gfx_boxto">gfx_BoxTo</h3>
<p>Draws a rectangle from the current origin to the new point using the current object colour. The top left corner is anchored by the current origin (x1, y1), the bottom right corner is specified by x2, y2.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_BoxTo(x2, y2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the diagonally opposed corner of the rectangle to be drawn, the top left corner (assumed to be x1, y1) is anchored by the current origin.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>

</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The default <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, however, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>SOLID</strong>, the rectangle will be drawn filled, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, the rectangle will be drawn as an outline. If the circle is drawn as <strong>SOLID</strong>, the outline colour can be specified with <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_OutlineColour(...)</strong></a>. If <strong>OUTLINE_COLOUR</strong> is set to 0, no outline is drawn.</p>
</div>

<h3 id="gfx_clipwindow">gfx_ClipWindow</h3>
<p>Specifies a clipping window region on the screen such that any objects and text placed onto the screen will be clipped and displayed only within that region. For the clipping window to take effect, "Clipping" setting must be enabled separately using <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_Set(CLIPPING, ON)</strong></a> or the shortcut <a href="#gfx_set"><strong>gfx_Clipping(ON)</strong></a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_ClipWindow(x1, y1, x2, y2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the top left corner of the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2,</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the bottom right corner of the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-73-1" name="__codelineno-73-1" href="#__codelineno-73-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">n</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-73-2" name="__codelineno-73-2" href="#__codelineno-73-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_ClipWindow</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-73-3" name="__codelineno-73-3" href="#__codelineno-73-3"></a><span class="nl">n</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50000</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-73-4" name="__codelineno-73-4" href="#__codelineno-73-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example will draw 50000 random colour pixels,</span>
<a id="__codelineno-73-5" name="__codelineno-73-5" href="#__codelineno-73-5"></a><span class="c1">// only the pixels within the clipping area will be visible.</span>

<a id="__codelineno-73-7" name="__codelineno-73-7" href="#__codelineno-73-7"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">gfx_PutPixel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="o">%</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="o">%</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">());</span>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_focuswindow">gfx_FocusWindow</h3>
<p>Sets the display hardware GRAM access registers to the clipping area ready for reading or writing. The function also returns the pixel count of the selected area.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_FocusWindow();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: The pixel count of the selected area.</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_set">gfx_Set</h3>
<p>Given a function number and a value, set the required graphics control parameter, such as size, colour, and other parameters. (see the <strong>Single parameter short-cuts for the gfx_Set functions</strong> below).</p>
<div class="admonition table">
<p class="admonition-title"><strong>Parameter/Function Table</strong></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">#</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Predefined Name</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Value</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">PEN_SIZE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set the draw mode for gfx_LineTo, gfx_LineRel, gfx_Dot, gfx_Bullet and gfx_BoxTo (default mode is OUTLINE) nb:- pen size is set to OUTLINE for normal operation</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>0</strong> or SOLID<br><strong>1</strong> or OUTLINE</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">BACKGROUND_COLOUR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set the screen background colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Colour, 0 - 65535</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">OBJECT_COLOUR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Generic colour for <a href="#gfx_lineto">gfx_LineTo(...)</a>, <a href="#gfx_linerel">gfx_LineRel(...)</a>, <a href="#gfx_dot">gfx_Dot()</a>, <a href="#gfx_bullet">gfx_Bullet(...)</a> and <a href="#gfx_boxto">gfx_BoxTo(...)</a></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Colour, 0 - 65535</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">CLIPPING</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Turns clipping on/off. The clipping points are set with <a href="#gfx_clipwindow">gfx_ClipWindow(...)</a></td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>0</strong> or ON<br><strong>1</strong> or OFF</td>
</tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">n/a</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">TRANSPARENCY</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Not implemented on GOLDELOX-GFX2</td>

</tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">Colour, 0 - 65535</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td style="text-align: center;">CONTRAST</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set contrast value, 0 = display off, 1-16 = contrast level ( only available on GOLDELOX Engineering samples, must be implemented in users code for GOLDELOX-GFX2 with external initialisation tables, refer to individual display driver data sheets)</td>

<h2 id="display-io-functions">Display I/O Functions</h2>
<p>These functions allow direct display access for fast blitting operations.</p>
<h3 id="disp_init">disp_Init</h3>
<p>The GOLDELOX-GFX2 needs to be aware of all the display registers and how to access them.
The initialisation and the state machine tables are necessary to achieve this.
Refer to the individual display data sheet available from the display manufacturer.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>For hardware platform modules such as uOLED-96-G1(GFX), uOLED-128-G1(GFX), etc the disp_Init(,,) is not needed. The modules are factory set-up with their display specific configurations.</p>
</div>
<p>** <em>Syntax</em> **:   <code>disp_Init(initTable, stateMachine);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">initTable</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A reference to the device initialisation table which is stored as a data statement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">stateMachine</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A reference to the device state machine table which is stored as a data statement.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-76-1" name="__codelineno-76-1" href="#__codelineno-76-1"></a><span class="c1">//============================================================================</span>
<a id="__codelineno-76-2" name="__codelineno-76-2" href="#__codelineno-76-2"></a><span class="c1">// SD1339 Device Initialisation Procedure</span>
<a id="__codelineno-76-3" name="__codelineno-76-3" href="#__codelineno-76-3"></a><span class="c1">//============================================================================</span>
<a id="__codelineno-76-4" name="__codelineno-76-4" href="#__codelineno-76-4"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-76-5" name="__codelineno-76-5" href="#__codelineno-76-5"></a><span class="cp">#DATA</span>
<a id="__codelineno-76-6" name="__codelineno-76-6" href="#__codelineno-76-6"></a><span class="n">byte</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">initTable</span>
<a id="__codelineno-76-7" name="__codelineno-76-7" href="#__codelineno-76-7"></a><span class="c1">// first 4 bytes of table hold</span>
<a id="__codelineno-76-8" name="__codelineno-76-8" href="#__codelineno-76-8"></a><span class="c1">// display access information</span>
<a id="__codelineno-76-9" name="__codelineno-76-9" href="#__codelineno-76-9"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">_DI</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SPLAY_X_MAX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">                </span><span class="c1">// width 1</span>
<a id="__codelineno-76-10" name="__codelineno-76-10" href="#__codelineno-76-10"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">_DISPLAY_X_MAX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">                 </span><span class="c1">// height 1</span>
<a id="__codelineno-76-11" name="__codelineno-76-11" href="#__codelineno-76-11"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">WRITE_GRAM</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">                     </span><span class="c1">// write access register</span>
<a id="__codelineno-76-12" name="__codelineno-76-12" href="#__codelineno-76-12"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">WRITE_GRAM</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w">                     </span><span class="c1">// read access register</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="disp_writecontrol">disp_WriteControl</h3>
<p>Sends a single byte (which is the lower 8 bits of <strong>value</strong>) to the display bus.
Refer to individual data sheets for the display for more information.
This function is used to extend the capabilities of the user code to gain access to the the display hardware.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>disp_WriteControl(value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the value to be written to the display control register. Only the lower 8 bits are sent to the display.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-77-1" name="__codelineno-77-1" href="#__codelineno-77-1"></a><span class="c1">// a function to utilise the hardware circle draw function</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="disp_writeword">disp_WriteWord</h3>
<p>Sends a 16 bit value to the display bus.
Since the GOLDELOX-GFX2 display data bus is 8bits wide, the HIGH byte is sent first followed by the LOW byte.
Refer to individual data sheets for the display for more information.
This function is used to extend the capabilities of the user code to gain access to the the display hardware.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>disp_WriteWord(value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the value to be written to the display data register. Only the lower 8 bits are sent to the display.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-79-1" name="__codelineno-79-1" href="#__codelineno-79-1"></a><span class="c1">// a function to utilise the hardware circle draw function</span>

<h3 id="disp_blitpixelsfrommedia">disp_BlitPixelsFromMedia</h3>
<p>Read the required number of pixels consecutively from the current media stream and write them to the current display GRAM address.
For 8bit colour mode, each pixel comprises a single 8bit value.
For 16bit colour, each pixel is composed of 2 bytes, the high order byte is read first, the low order bye is read next.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>disp_BlitPixelsFromMedia(pixelcount);</code></p>

<td style="text-align: left;">Specifying the number of pixels to be consecutively read from the media stream.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>

<h3 id="disp_blitpixelsfromcom">disp_BlitPixelsFromCOM</h3>
<p>Fills a preselected GRAM screen area with the specified colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>disp_BlitPixelsFromCOM(mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">mode = 0 - specifies 16 bit pixels mode = pointer : specifies pointer to 16 element colour lookup table for each 4bit pixel value</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>

<a id="__codelineno-88-39" name="__codelineno-88-39" href="#__codelineno-88-39"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">gfx_FocusWindow</span><span class="p">();</span>

<h2 class="page-break" id="media-sdsdhc-card-or-serial-flash-chip-functions">Media (SD/SDHC card or Serial Flash chip) Functions</h2>
<p>The media can be SD/SDHC, microSD or serial (NAND) flash device interfaced to the GOLDELOX-GFX2 SPI port.</p>
<h3 id="media_init">media_Init</h3>
<p>Initialise a uSD/SD/SDHC memory card for further operations. The SD card is connected to the SPI (serial peripheral interface) of the GOLDELOX-GFX2 chip.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Init();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>1</strong> if memory card is present and successfully initialised</li>
<li><strong>0</strong> if no card is present or not able to initialise</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-89-1" name="__codelineno-89-1" href="#__codelineno-89-1"></a><span class="c1">// Waits for SD card to be inserted and initialised, flashing a message if no SD card detected.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-89-2" name="__codelineno-89-2" href="#__codelineno-89-2"></a><span class="k">while</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">media_Init</span><span class="p">())</span>
<a id="__codelineno-89-3" name="__codelineno-89-3" href="#__codelineno-89-3"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-89-4" name="__codelineno-89-4" href="#__codelineno-89-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">300</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-89-5" name="__codelineno-89-5" href="#__codelineno-89-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="err">“</span><span class="n">Please</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">insert</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SD</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">card</span><span class="err">”</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-89-6" name="__codelineno-89-6" href="#__codelineno-89-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">300</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-89-7" name="__codelineno-89-7" href="#__codelineno-89-7"></a><span class="n">wend</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The media can be SD/SDHC, microSD or serial (NAND) flash device interfaced to the GOLDELOX-GFX2 SPI port.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="media_setadd">media_SetAdd</h3>
<p>Set media memory internal Address pointer for access at a non sector aligned byte address.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_SetAdd(HIword, LOword);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HIword</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the high word (upper 2 bytes) of a 4 byte media memory byte address location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LOword</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the low word (lower 2 bytes) of a 4 byte media memory byte address location.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-90-1" name="__codelineno-90-1" href="#__codelineno-90-1"></a><span class="c1">// sets the media address to byte 513 (which is sector #1, 2nd byte in sector) for subsequent operations.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-90-2" name="__codelineno-90-2" href="#__codelineno-90-2"></a><span class="n">media_SetAdd</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">513</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="media_setsector">media_SetSector</h3>
<p>Set media memory internal Address pointer for sector access.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_SetSector(HIword, LOword);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HIword</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the high word (upper 2 bytes) of a 4 byte media memory byte address location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LOword</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the low word (lower 2 bytes) of a 4 byte media memory byte address location.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-91-1" name="__codelineno-91-1" href="#__codelineno-91-1"></a><span class="c1">// Sets the media address to the 11th sector for subsequent operations</span>
<a id="__codelineno-91-2" name="__codelineno-91-2" href="#__codelineno-91-2"></a><span class="c1">// (which is also byte address 5120)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-91-3" name="__codelineno-91-3" href="#__codelineno-91-3"></a><span class="n">media_SetSector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="media_readbyte">media_ReadByte</h3>
<p>Returns the byte value from the current media address. The internal byte address will then be internally incremented by one.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_ReadByte();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  byte value</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-92-1" name="__codelineno-92-1" href="#__codelineno-92-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">LObyte</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">HIbyte</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-92-2" name="__codelineno-92-2" href="#__codelineno-92-2"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">media_Init</span><span class="p">())</span><span class="w">                       </span><span class="c1">// initialises the media</span>
<a id="__codelineno-92-3" name="__codelineno-92-3" href="#__codelineno-92-3"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">media_SetAdd</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">510</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">               </span><span class="c1">// sets the media byte address to 510</span>
<a id="__codelineno-92-4" name="__codelineno-92-4" href="#__codelineno-92-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">LObyte</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">media_ReadByte</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// reads the last 2 bytes from sector 0</span>
<a id="__codelineno-92-5" name="__codelineno-92-5" href="#__codelineno-92-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">HIbyte</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">media_ReadByte</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-92-6" name="__codelineno-92-6" href="#__codelineno-92-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">HEX2</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">HIbyte</span><span class="p">,[</span><span class="n">HEX2</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">LObyte</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-92-7" name="__codelineno-92-7" href="#__codelineno-92-7"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// If the card happens to be FAT formatted, the result will be “AA55”.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-92-8" name="__codelineno-92-8" href="#__codelineno-92-8"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// The media internal address is internally incremented for each of the byte operations.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-92-9" name="__codelineno-92-9" href="#__codelineno-92-9"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
<a id="__codelineno-92-10" name="__codelineno-92-10" href="#__codelineno-92-10"></a><span class="n">repeat</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">forever</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="media_readword">media_ReadWord</h3>
<p>Returns the word value (2 bytes) from the current media address. The internal byte address will then be internally incremented by one. If the address is not aligned, the word will still be read correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_ReadWord();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   word value</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-93-1" name="__codelineno-93-1" href="#__codelineno-93-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myword</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-93-2" name="__codelineno-93-2" href="#__codelineno-93-2"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">media_Init</span><span class="p">())</span><span class="w">               </span><span class="c1">// initialises the media</span>
<a id="__codelineno-93-3" name="__codelineno-93-3" href="#__codelineno-93-3"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">media_SetAdd</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">510</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="c1">// sets the media byte address to 510</span>
<a id="__codelineno-93-4" name="__codelineno-93-4" href="#__codelineno-93-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">myword</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">media_ReadWord</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// reads the last word from sector 0</span>
<a id="__codelineno-93-5" name="__codelineno-93-5" href="#__codelineno-93-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">HEX4</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">myword</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// If the card happens to be formatted, the result will be “AA55”</span>
<a id="__codelineno-93-6" name="__codelineno-93-6" href="#__codelineno-93-6"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
<a id="__codelineno-93-7" name="__codelineno-93-7" href="#__codelineno-93-7"></a><span class="n">repeat</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">forever</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="media_writebyte">media_WriteByte</h3>
<p>Writes a byte to the current media address that was initially set with <strong>media_SetSector(...);</strong></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_WriteByte(byte_val);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">byte_val</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The lower 8 bits specifies the byte to be written at the current media address location.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: Non zero if write was successful.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-94-1" name="__codelineno-94-1" href="#__codelineno-94-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example initialises the media, writes some bytes to the required sector,</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-2" name="__codelineno-94-2" href="#__codelineno-94-2"></a><span class="c1">// then prints the result from the required location.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-3" name="__codelineno-94-3" href="#__codelineno-94-3"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">n</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-4" name="__codelineno-94-4" href="#__codelineno-94-4"></a><span class="k">while</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">media_Init</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="o">==</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">            </span><span class="c1">// wait if no SD card detected</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-5" name="__codelineno-94-5" href="#__codelineno-94-5"></a><span class="n">media_SetSector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">              </span><span class="c1">// at sector 2</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-6" name="__codelineno-94-6" href="#__codelineno-94-6"></a><span class="c1">//media_SetAdd(0, 1024);            // (alternatively, use media_SetAdd(),</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-7" name="__codelineno-94-7" href="#__codelineno-94-7"></a><span class="w">                                    </span><span class="c1">// lower 9 bits</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-8" name="__codelineno-94-8" href="#__codelineno-94-8"></a><span class="k">while</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-9" name="__codelineno-94-9" href="#__codelineno-94-9"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">media_WriteByte</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">++</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">+</span><span class="sc">'0'</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">// write ASCII '0123456789' to the</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-10" name="__codelineno-94-10" href="#__codelineno-94-10"></a><span class="n">wend</span><span class="w">                                </span><span class="c1">// first 10 locations.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-11" name="__codelineno-94-11" href="#__codelineno-94-11"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-94-12" name="__codelineno-94-12" href="#__codelineno-94-12"></a><span class="nf">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">MDA</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Hello World"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// now write a ascii test string</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-13" name="__codelineno-94-13" href="#__codelineno-94-13"></a><span class="n">media_WriteByte</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sc">'A'</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">               </span><span class="c1">// write a further 3 bytes</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-14" name="__codelineno-94-14" href="#__codelineno-94-14"></a><span class="n">media_WriteByte</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sc">'B'</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-15" name="__codelineno-94-15" href="#__codelineno-94-15"></a><span class="n">media_WriteByte</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sc">'C'</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-16" name="__codelineno-94-16" href="#__codelineno-94-16"></a><span class="n">media_WriteByte</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                 </span><span class="c1">// terminate with zero</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-17" name="__codelineno-94-17" href="#__codelineno-94-17"></a><span class="n">media_Flush</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">                      </span><span class="c1">// we're finished, close the sector</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-18" name="__codelineno-94-18" href="#__codelineno-94-18"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-94-19" name="__codelineno-94-19" href="#__codelineno-94-19"></a><span class="n">media_SetAdd</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1024</span><span class="o">+</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">            </span><span class="c1">// set the starting byte address</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-20" name="__codelineno-94-20" href="#__codelineno-94-20"></a><span class="k">while</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="n">media_ReadByte</span><span class="p">())</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putch</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// print result, starting</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-21" name="__codelineno-94-21" href="#__codelineno-94-21"></a><span class="w">                                            </span><span class="c1">// from '5'</span>
<a id="__codelineno-94-22" name="__codelineno-94-22" href="#__codelineno-94-22"></a><span class="n">repeat</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">forever</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Due to design constraints on the GOLDELOX-GFX2, there is no way of writing bytes or words within a media sector without starting from the beginning of the sector. All writes will start at the beginning of a sector and are incremental until the <a href="#media_flush"><strong>media_Flush()</strong></a> function is executed, or the sector address rolls over to the next sector. Any remaining bytes in the sector will be padded with <strong>0xFF</strong>, destroying the previous contents. An attempt to use the <a href="#media_setadd"><strong>media_SetAdd(..)</strong></a> function will result in the lower 9 bits being interpreted as zero. If the writing rolls over to the next sector, the media_Flush() function is issued automatically internally.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="media_writeword">media_WriteWord</h3>
<p>Writes a byte to the current media address that was initially set with <a href="#media_setsector"><strong>media_SetSector(...)</strong></a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_WriteWord(word_val);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">word_val</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The 16 bit word to be written at the current media address location.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Non zero if write was successful.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-95-19" name="__codelineno-95-19" href="#__codelineno-95-19"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">HEX4</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">media_ReadWord</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="s">" n"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-95-20" name="__codelineno-95-20" href="#__codelineno-95-20"></a><span class="n">wend</span>
<a id="__codelineno-95-21" name="__codelineno-95-21" href="#__codelineno-95-21"></a><span class="n">repeat</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">forever</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Due to design constraints on the GOLDELOX-GFX2, there is no way of writing bytes or words within a media sector without starting from the beginning of the sector. All writes will start at the beginning of a sector and are incremental until the <a href="#media_flush"><strong>media_Flush()</strong></a> function is executed, or the sector address rolls over to the next sector. Any remaining bytes in the sector will be padded with <strong>0xFF</strong>, destroying the previous contents. An attempt to use the <a href="#media_setadd"><strong>media_SetAdd(..)</strong></a> function will result in the lower 9 bits being interpreted as zero. If the writing rolls over to the next sector, the media_Flush() function is issued automatically internally.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="media_flush">media_Flush</h3>
<p>After writing any data to a sector, media_Flush() should be called to ensure that the current sector that is being written is correctly stored back to the media else write operations may be unpredictable.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Flush();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<p>See the <a href="#media_writebyte">media_WriteByte(..)</a> and <a href="#media_writeword">media_WriteWord(..)</a> examples.</p>
<h3 id="media_image">media_Image</h3>
<p>Displays an image from the media storage at the specified co-ordinates. The image address is previously specified with the <a href="#media_setadd"><strong>media_SetAdd(..)</strong></a> or <a href="#media_setsector">**media_SetSector(...)</a> function**. If the image is shown partially off screen, it is necessary to enable clipping for it to be displayed correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Image(x, y);</code></p>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="media_video">media_Video</h3>
<p>Displays a <em>video</em> clip from the media storage device at the specified co-ordinates. If the <em>video</em> is shown partially off screen, it is necessary to enable clipping for it be displayed correctly. Note that showing a <em>video</em> blocks all other processes until the video has finished showing. See the <a href="#media_videoframe"><strong>media_VideoFrame(...)</strong></a> functions for alternatives.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Video(x, y);</code></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="media_videoframe">media_VideoFrame</h3>
<p>Displays a <em>video</em> from the media storage device at the specified co-ordinates. This function gives you great flexibility for showing various icons from an image strip, as well as showing videos while doing other tasks</p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="flash-memory-chip-functions">Flash Memory Chip Functions</h2>
<p>The functions in this section only apply to serial SPI (NAND) flash devices interfaced to the GOLDELOX-GFX2 SPI port.</p>
<h3 id="flash_sig">flash_SIG</h3>
<p>If a FLASH storage device is connected to the SPI port, and has been correctly initialised with the <a href="#spi_init">spi_Init(...)</a> function, the Electronic Signature of the device can be read using this function. The only devices supported so far on the GOLDELOX-GFX2 are the M25Pxx range of devices which are 512Kbit to 32Mbit (2M x 8) Serial Flash Memory.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_SIG();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Release from Deep Power-down, and Read Electronic Signature. Only the low order byte is valid, the upper byte is ignored.</p>
<!-- TODO: Add example -->

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This functions only apply to serial SPI (NAND) flash devices interfaced to the GOLDELOX-GFX2 SPI port.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="flash_id">flash_ID</h3>
<p>If a FLASH storage device is connected to the SPI port, and has been correctly initialised with the <a href="#spi_init">spi_Init(...)</a> function, the memory type and capacity from the flash device can be read using this function. The only devices supported so far on the GOLDELOX-GFX2 are the M25Pxx range of devices which are 512Kbit to 32Mbit (2M x 8) Serial Flash Memory.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_ID();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Reads the memory type and capacity from the serial FLASH device. Hi byte contains type, and low byte contains capacity. Refer to the device data sheet for further information.  </p>
<!-- TODO: Add example -->

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This functions only apply to serial SPI (NAND) flash devices interfaced to the GOLDELOX-GFX2 SPI port.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="flash_bulkerase">flash_BulkErase</h3>
<p>If a FLASH storage device is connected to the SPI port, and has been correctly initialised with the <a href="#spi_init">spi_Init(...)</a> function, the FLASH device can be completely erased using this function. The only devices supported so far on the GOLDELOX-GFX2 are the M25Pxx range of devices which are 512Kbit to 32Mbit (2M x 8) Serial Flash Memory.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_BulkErase();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<!-- TODO: Add example -->

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This functions only apply to serial SPI (NAND) flash devices interfaced to the GOLDELOX-GFX2 SPI port.</li>
<li>Erases the entire flash media device. The function returns no value, and the operation can take up to 80 seconds depending on the size of the flash device.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<h3 id="flash_blockerase">flash_BlockErase</h3>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_BlockErase(blockAddress);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">blockAddress</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The address of the 64k FLASH block to be erased.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Erases the required block in a FLASH media device. The function returns no value, and the operation can take up to 3 milliseconds.</p>
<!-- TODO: Add example -->

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This functions only apply to serial SPI (NAND) flash devices interfaced to the GOLDELOX-GFX2 SPI port.</p>
</div>
<h2 class="page-break" id="spi-control-functions">SPI Control Functions</h2>
<p>The SPI functions in this section apply to any general-purpose SPI device.</p>
<h3 id="spi_init">spi_Init</h3>
<p>Sets up the GOLDELOX-GFX2 SPI port to communicate with SPI devices.</p>
<p><img alt="spi_Init" class="width-50 pdf-width-70" src="../img/goldelox/image4.jpeg"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Init(speed, input_mode, output_mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the speed of the SPI port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">input_mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the input mode of the SPI port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">output_mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the output mode of the SPI port.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The SPI functions in this section are not necessary when using the memory card or serial flash chips interfaced to the SPI port.
The SPI functions in this section are relevant to those devices other than the memory card and the serial flash chip used for media access.</p>
</div>
<!--TODO: Add example-->

<h3 id="spi_read">spi_Read</h3>
<p>This function allows a raw unadorned byte read from the SPI device.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Read();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Returns a single data byte from the SPI device.</p>
<!--TODO: Add example-->

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The Chip Select line (SDCS) is lowered automatically.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="spi_write">spi_Write</h3>
<p>This function allows a raw unadorned byte write to the SPI device.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Write(byte);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the data byte to be sent to the SPI device.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>
<!--TODO: Add example-->

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The Chip Select line (SDCS) is lowered automatically.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="spi_disable">spi_Disable</h3>
<p>This function raises the Chip Select (SDCS) line of the SPI device, disabling it from further activity. The CS line will be automatically lowered next time the SPI functions spi_Read() or spi_Write(...) are used, and also by action of any of the media_ functions.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Disable();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>
<!--TODO: Add example-->

<h2 class="page-break" id="serial-uart-communication-functions">Serial (UART) Communication Functions</h2>
<h3 id="serin">serin</h3>
<p>Receives a character from the Serial Port COM0. The transmission format is:
<strong>No Parity, 1 Stop Bit, 8 Data Bits</strong> (N,8,1).
The default Baud Rate is 115,200 bits per second or 115,200 baud. The baud rate can be changed under program control by using the <a href="#setbaud"><strong>setbaud(...)</strong></a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>serin();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>-1</strong> if no character is available</li>
<li><strong>-2</strong> if a framing error or over-run has occurred (auto cleared)</li>
<li><strong>0 or a positive value</strong> (up to 255) for a valid character received </li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-100-1" name="__codelineno-100-1" href="#__codelineno-100-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-100-2" name="__codelineno-100-2" href="#__codelineno-100-2"></a><span class="nl">char</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">serin</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">            </span><span class="c1">// test the com port</span>
<a id="__codelineno-100-3" name="__codelineno-100-3" href="#__codelineno-100-3"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&gt;=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">              </span><span class="c1">// if a valid character is received</span>
<a id="__codelineno-100-4" name="__codelineno-100-4" href="#__codelineno-100-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">process</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">          </span><span class="c1">// process the character</span>
<a id="__codelineno-100-5" name="__codelineno-100-5" href="#__codelineno-100-5"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="serout">serout</h3>
<p>Transmits a single byte from the Serial Port COM0. The transmission format is: <strong>No Parity, 1 Stop Bit, 8 Data Bits</strong> (N,8,1).
The default Baud Rate is 115,200 bits per second or 115,200 baud. The baud rate can be changed under program control by using the <a href="#setbaud"><strong>setbaud(...)</strong></a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>serout(char);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the data byte to be sent to the serial port.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<!-- TODO: Add example -->

<p>The baud rate divisor is calculated with the following formula, and can be used when non-constant defined baud rates are required:</p>
<dl>
<dt><strong>Rate Divisor = (3000000 / baud ) – 1</strong></dt>
<dd>
<p>The rate divisor of 200000baud for example, would be (3000000/200000)-1 = 14, so setbaud(14) will give you 200K baud rate.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
<p>Baud rates each have degree of accuracy for several reasons. The actual baud rate you would receive and relevant error% compared to the setting value, can be calculated.</p>
<dl>
<dt><strong>ActualBaud = 3000000/(trunc(3000000/RequiredBaud))</strong></dt>
<dd>
<p>Example for 115200 is, 3000000/115200 = 26.041, Trucated is 26. 3000000/26 = 115384 (rounded). Error% therefore is % difference between 115200 and 115384, therefore 0.16%
It is desirable to only use a baud rate between 2 devices which has a difference of typically &lt; 2%. Note both devices will have a degree of error, not just this 4D Processor, both need to be considered.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>setbaud(rate);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">rate</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the baud rate divisor value or pre-defined constant</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>

<h3 id="com_autobaud">com_AutoBaud</h3>
<p>The com_AutoBaud function expects to receive an ascii 'U' (0x55) within a pre-determined time. If the function is successful, the COM port is configured to the closest speed possible, and the selected baud rate value is returned.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_AutoBaud(timeout);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">timeout</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the timeout delay for autobaud detection.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The divisor value selected for the baud rate generator, else returns 0.   </p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="com_init">com_Init</h3>
<p>This is the initialisation function for the serial communications buffered service. Once initialised, the service runs in the background capturing and buffering serial data without the user application having to constantly poll the serial port. This frees up the application to service other tasks. The service also transparently keeps a checksum (see the <a href="#com_checksum"><strong>com_Checksum()</strong></a> function) which can be employed if required for robust error checking.</p>
<p><strong>MODES OF OPERATION</strong></p>
<dl>
<dt><strong>No qualifier – simple ring buffer (aka circular queue)</strong></dt>
<dd>
<p>If the <strong>qualifier</strong> is set to zero, the <strong>buffer</strong> is continually active as a simple circular queue. Characters when received from the host are placed in the circular queue (at the 'head' of the queue) Bytes may be removed from the circular queue (from the 'tail' of the queue) using the <a href="#serin"><strong>serin()</strong></a> function. If the tail is the same position as the head, there are no bytes in the queue, therefore <a href="#serin"><strong>serin()</strong></a> will return <strong>-1</strong>, meaning no character is available, also, the <a href="#com_count"><strong>com_Count()</strong></a> function can be read at any time to determine the number of characters that are waiting between the tail and head of the queue. If the queue is not read frequently by the application, and characters are still being sent by the host, the head will eventually catch up with the tail setting the internal COM_FULL flag (which can be read with the <a href="#com_full"><strong>com_Full()</strong></a> function) . Any further characters from the host are are now discarded, however, all the characters that were buffered up to this point are readable. This is a good way of reading a fixed size packet and not necessarily considered to be an error condition. If no characters are removed from the buffer until the COM_FULL flag (which can be read with the <a href="#com_full"><strong>com_Full()</strong></a> function) becomes set, it is guaranteed that the bytes will be ordered in the <strong>buffer</strong> from the start position, therefore, the <strong>buffer</strong> can be treated as an array and can be read directly without using <a href="#serin"><strong>serin()</strong></a> at all. In the latter case, the correct action is to process the data from the buffer, re-initialise the buffer with the <a href="#com_init"><strong>com_Init(..)</strong></a> function, or reset the buffered serial service by issuing the <a href="#com_reset"><strong>com_Reset()</strong></a> function (which will return serial reception to polled mode) , and send an acknowledgement to the host (traditionally a <strong>ACK</strong> or 6) to indicate that the application is ready to receive more data and the previous 'packet' has been dealt with, or conversely, the application may send a negative acknowledgement to indicate that some sort of error occurred, or the action could not be completed (traditionally a <strong>NAK</strong> or 15) .</p>
<p>If any low level errors occur during the buffering service (such as framing or over-run) the internal COM_ERROR flag will be set (which can be read with the <a href="#com_error"><strong>com_Error()</strong></a> function). </p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The COM_FULL flag will remain latched to indicate that the buffer did become full, and is not reset (even if all the characters are read) until the <a href="#com_init">com_Init(..)</a> or <a href="#com_reset">com_Reset()</a> function is issued.</p>
</div>
</dd>
</dl>
<p class="page-break"></p>

<dl>
<dt><strong>Using a qualifier</strong></dt>
<dd>
<p>If a <strong>qualifier</strong> character is specified, after the buffer is initialised with <a href="#com_init"><strong>com_Init(..)</strong></a> , the service will ignore all characters until the <strong>qualifier</strong> is received and only then initiate the buffer write sequence with incoming data. After that point, the behaviour is the same as above for the 'non qualified' mode.</p>
</dd>
<dt><strong>Variable packet length</strong></dt>
<dd>
<p>If the <strong>bufsize</strong> argument is set to zero, the first byte received (or the 2nd byte if a <strong>qualifier</strong> is employed) sets the count of characters that are to be received before the COM_FULL flag (which can be read with the <a href="#com_full"><strong>com_Full()</strong></a> function) becomes set. This allows a host to send variable length packets, which will only alert the application that the packet is ready after the correct number of characters has been received. The number of bytes to be expected can be read using the <a href="#com_packetsize"><strong>com_PacketSize()</strong></a> function, which will indicate the packet size. In this mode, it is wise to make the buffer as large as possible due to the fact that if the 'size' parameter sent by the host is corrupted, more characters than expected (up to 255) can be receive inadvertently, crashing into any other program variables above the array.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">buffer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the address of a buffer used for the background buffering service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the byte size of the user array provided for the buffer (each array element holds 2 bytes). If the buffer size is zero, a buffer of 63 words (126 bytes) should be provided for automatic packet length mode (see below). Buffer of 63 words (126 bytes) is the maximum buffer size possible.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">qualifier</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the qualifying character that must be received to initiate serial data reception and buffer write. A zero (0x00) indicates no qualifier to be used.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
