<a id="__codelineno-106-26" name="__codelineno-106-26" href="#__codelineno-106-26"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">com_Count "</span><span class="p">,[</span><span class="n">DEC2ZB</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com_Count</span><span class="p">());</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// show count</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-27" name="__codelineno-106-27" href="#__codelineno-106-27"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">com_Checksum "</span><span class="p">,[</span><span class="n">HEX2ZB</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com_Checksum</span><span class="p">());</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="c1">// checksum</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-28" name="__codelineno-106-28" href="#__codelineno-106-28"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">com_Full "</span><span class="p">,[</span><span class="n">DEC2ZB</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com_Full</span><span class="p">());</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="c1">// 1 if full</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-29" name="__codelineno-106-29" href="#__codelineno-106-29"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1000</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                                        </span><span class="c1">// a delay to slow things up</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-30" name="__codelineno-106-30" href="#__codelineno-106-30"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">until</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">com_Full</span><span class="p">());</span><span class="w">                                      </span><span class="c1">// just loop until buffer is full</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-31" name="__codelineno-106-31" href="#__codelineno-106-31"></a><span class="w">            </span><span class="c1">// buffer is full, echo the characters</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-32" name="__codelineno-106-32" href="#__codelineno-106-32"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="k">while</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">chr</span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="n">serin</span><span class="p">())</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&gt;=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">serout</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">chr</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">              </span><span class="c1">// echo back the chars</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-33" name="__codelineno-106-33" href="#__codelineno-106-33"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">COM0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">" OK n"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                               </span><span class="c1">// send a simple acknowledgement</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-34" name="__codelineno-106-34" href="#__codelineno-106-34"></a><span class="n">forever</span><span class="w">                                                     </span><span class="c1">// do it all ag ain</span>
</code></pre></div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--prev" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div><div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--next" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Transparent to normal operation, a check summing system is operating. If the host sends one extra character (usually at the end of the packet) which is the negated value of the addition of all the previous characters in the packet , the checksum (which can be read with the <a href="#com_checksum"><strong>com_Checksum()</strong></a> function) should read zero. <a href="#com_checksum"><strong>com_Checksum()</strong></a> will retain the most recent value until <a href="#com_init"><strong>com_Init(..)</strong></a> is called again to reset the buffer system. Note that the checksum is only valid after the <a href="#com_full"><strong>com_Full()</strong></a> function reports a buffer full situation (ie the packet is fully received).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="#com_packetsize"><strong>com_PacketSize()</strong></a> will indicate how large the packet is ONLY after the packet reception has started. Although it is usually not required to know the packet size until the packet has actually been read, if it is a requirement, the count is available as soon as <a href="#com_count"><strong>com_Count()</strong></a> becomes non zero.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="com_reset">com_Reset</h3>
<p>Resets the serial communications buffered service and returns it to the default polled mode.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Reset();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Retruns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-107-1" name="__codelineno-107-1" href="#__codelineno-107-1"></a><span class="n">com_Reset</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// reset to polled mode</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_count">com_Count</h3>
<p>Can be read at any time (when in buffered communications is active) to determine the number of characters that are waiting in the buffer.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Count();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Current count of characters in the communications buffer. </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-108-1" name="__codelineno-108-1" href="#__codelineno-108-1"></a><span class="nl">n</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com_Count</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// get the number of chars available in the buffer</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_full">com_Full</h3>
<p>If the queue is not read frequently by the application, and characters are still being sent by the host, the head will eventually catch up with the tail setting the COM_FULL flag which is read with this function. If this flag is set, any further characters from the host are discarded, however, all the characters that were buffered up to this point are readable.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Full();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  <strong>1</strong> if buffer or queue has become full, or is overflowed, else returns <strong>0</strong></p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-109-1" name="__codelineno-109-1" href="#__codelineno-109-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">com_Full</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">com_Count</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">==</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-109-2" name="__codelineno-109-2" href="#__codelineno-109-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">com_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="c1">// buffer full, recovery</span>
<a id="__codelineno-109-3" name="__codelineno-109-3" href="#__codelineno-109-3"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="com_error">com_Error</h3>
<p>If any low level errors occur during the buffering service (such as framing or over-run) the internal <strong>COM_ERROR</strong> flag will be set which can be read with this function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Error();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  <strong>1</strong> if any low level communications error occurred, else returns <strong>0</strong></p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-110-1" name="__codelineno-110-1" href="#__codelineno-110-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">com_Error</span><span class="p">())</span><span class="w">                     </span><span class="c1">// if there were low level comms errors,</span>
<a id="__codelineno-110-2" name="__codelineno-110-2" href="#__codelineno-110-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">resetMySystem</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">                </span><span class="c1">// take corrective action</span>
<a id="__codelineno-110-3" name="__codelineno-110-3" href="#__codelineno-110-3"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_sync">com_Sync</h3>
<p>If a <strong><em>qualifier</em></strong> character is specified when using buffered communications, after the buffer is initialized with <a href="#com_init"><strong>com_Init(..)</strong></a> , the service will ignore all characters until the <strong><em>qualifier</em></strong> is received and only then initiate the buffer write sequence with incoming data. <a href="#com_sync"><strong>com_Sync()</strong></a> is called to determine if the qualifier character has been received yet.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Sync();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: <strong>1</strong> if the qualifier character has been received, else returns <strong>0</strong>.   </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-111-1" name="__codelineno-111-1" href="#__codelineno-111-1"></a><span class="n">com_Sync</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// reset to polled mode</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="com_checksum">com_Checksum</h3>
<p>Transparent to normal operation, a check summing system is operating. If the host sends one extra character as part of the packet (usually added at the end of the packet) which is the negated value of the addition of all the previous characters in the packet. Once the <a href="#com_full"><strong>com_Full()</strong></a> function reports a buffer full situation (ie the packet is fully received) , the checksum can be read, and should read zero if the packet is not corrupted.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Checksum();</code> </p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if checksum has been computed correctly.    </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-112-1" name="__codelineno-112-1" href="#__codelineno-112-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">com_Checksum</span><span class="p">())</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// if checksum is ok</span>
<a id="__codelineno-112-2" name="__codelineno-112-2" href="#__codelineno-112-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">processMyPacket</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">// continue</span>
<a id="__codelineno-112-3" name="__codelineno-112-3" href="#__codelineno-112-3"></a><span class="k">else</span>
<a id="__codelineno-112-4" name="__codelineno-112-4" href="#__codelineno-112-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// do recovery action</span>
<a id="__codelineno-112-5" name="__codelineno-112-5" href="#__codelineno-112-5"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_packetsize">com_PacketSize</h3>
<p><a href="#com_packetsize"><strong>com_PacketSize()</strong></a> will indicate how large the packet is ONLY after the packet reception has started. Although it is usually not required to know the packet size until the packet has actually been read, if it is a requirement, the count is available as soon as <a href="#com_count"><strong>com_Count()</strong></a> becomes non zero. If not in variable packet length mode, <a href="#com_packetsize"><strong>com_PacketSize()</strong></a> just returns the size of the specified buffer.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_PacketSize();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The size of a packet if in variable packet length mode, or just the size of the serial buffer if not variable packet length mode.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-113-1" name="__codelineno-113-1" href="#__codelineno-113-1"></a><span class="n">If</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">com_Count</span><span class="p">())</span>
<a id="__codelineno-113-2" name="__codelineno-113-2" href="#__codelineno-113-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Waiting...."</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-113-3" name="__codelineno-113-3" href="#__codelineno-113-3"></a><span class="k">else</span>
<a id="__codelineno-113-4" name="__codelineno-113-4" href="#__codelineno-113-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">com_PacketSize</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com_Count</span><span class="p">()),</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">bytes</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">to</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">go</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">""</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span>
<a id="__codelineno-113-5" name="__codelineno-113-5" href="#__codelineno-113-5"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 class="page-break" id="sound-and-tune-rtttl-functions">Sound and Tune (RTTTL) Functions</h2>
<h3 id="tune_play">tune_Play</h3>
<p>This function uses a variant of "Ring Tone Text Transfer Language" (RTTTL) developed by Nokia for ring tones. There are differences that need to be taken into account, and several additions that can be utilised. It is suggested to refer to the original format first. Here are some useful discussions:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_Tone_Transfer_Language">http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_Tone_Transfer_Language</a> and;</li>
<li><a href="https://www.mobilefish.com/tutorials/rtttl/rtttl_quickguide_specification.html">https://www.mobilefish.com/tutorials/rtttl/rtttl_quickguide_specification.html</a></li>
</ul>
<p>With a little practice and minor modifications, most RTTTL tunes that can be downloaded off the web are playable with this function.
Also, a wide range of sound effects can be made using standard RTTTL notation augmented with the additional 4DGL functions.</p>
<p><strong>The 4DGL implementation:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>
<p>The "b=nnn" in 4DGL does not represent "beats per minute" (bpm), it represents "milliseconds per hemidemisemiquaver".</p>
<p><strong>e.g.</strong> 120 bpm is 2 beats per second = 128 demisemiquavers per second which is 7.8125msec per hemidemisemiquaver. Conversely, the default 4DGL value for b = 16msec per hemidemisemiquaver equates to 62.5 bpm.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>The original RTTTL format is a string divided into three sections: <em>name, default value and data</em>.
    While the 4DGL implementation <strong>does not have</strong> the <strong>name</strong> section.</p>
</li>
<li>The 4DGL implementation does not require any spaces or colons anywhere.</li>
<li>The 4DGL implementation allows default values to be changed anywhere in the string and does not need to be at the start.</li>
<li>
<p>The optional default modifiers is a set of parameters separated by commas, where each value contains a key and a value separated by an '=' character, which describes certain defaults which will be adhered to during the execution of the ringtone string.</p>
<p><strong>d</strong> - duration, can be one of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64 (64 = 1/64th, 1 = 1 whole unit).</p>
<ul>
<li>1 specifies a Semibreve (Whole Note),</li>
<li>2 indicates it a Minim (Half Note),</li>
<li>4 is a Crotchet (Quarter Note) etc up to 64 which is a hemidemisemiquaver (64th note).</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>b</strong> - beat/tempo in milliseconds per demisemiquaver</p>
<p><strong>o</strong> - octave (scale) can be 4, 5, 6, or 7.</p>
<p>If not specified, defaults are:</p>
<ul>
<li>duration = 4 (same as d=4)</li>
<li>octave = 6 (same as o=6)</li>
<li>beat = 16 (same as b=16) close to 63bpm</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<dl>
<dt><strong>4DGL extended default values:</strong></dt>
<dd>
<p><strong>r</strong> - set repeat point and counter (eg r=4)</p>
<ul>
<li>min = 2, max = 255</li>
<li>default value = forever</li>
</ul>
</dd>
<dd>
<p><strong>p</strong> - set portamento value (eg p=5)</p>
<ul>
<li>min = 1, max = 14</li>
<li>default value is 4</li>
</ul>
</dd>
<dd>
<p><strong>a</strong> - set arpeggiation step value (eg a=1)</p>
<ul>
<li>min = 1, max = 16</li>
<li>default value is 1</li>
</ul>
</dd>
<dt><strong>4DGL extended commands associated with extended default values:</strong></dt>
<dd>
<p><strong>R</strong> - execute a repeat specified by <code>r=</code>. If no repeat count has been specified, the string will repeat forever</p>
</dd>
<dd>
<p><strong>{</strong> - turn portamento ON</p>
</dd>
<dd>
<p><strong>}</strong> - turn portamento OFF (default)</p>
</dd>
<dd>
<p><strong>+</strong> - raise note as specified by arpeggiation step value</p>
</dd>
<dd>
<p><strong>-</strong> - lower note as specified by arpeggiation step value</p>
</dd>
</dl>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>tune_Play(tuneptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">tuneptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies a pointer to a data statement or a string constant containing RTTTL information.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The argument passed to the tune_Play(...) function must be an ASCII string.
If the string is passed as a pointer from a <code>#DATA</code> statement, it must be terminated with a zero (0x00).
If a string is passed directly as a parameter, the '0' is automatically appended by the compiler as per normal strings.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p class="page-break"></p>

<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-114-1" name="__codelineno-114-1" href="#__codelineno-114-1"></a><span class="cm">/*</span>
<a id="__codelineno-114-2" name="__codelineno-114-2" href="#__codelineno-114-2"></a><span class="cm"> * This example shows how to use the RTTTL tunes to</span>
<a id="__codelineno-114-3" name="__codelineno-114-3" href="#__codelineno-114-3"></a><span class="cm"> * generate complex sounds and music.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-114-4" name="__codelineno-114-4" href="#__codelineno-114-4"></a><span class="cm">*/</span>
<a id="__codelineno-114-5" name="__codelineno-114-5" href="#__codelineno-114-5"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-114-6" name="__codelineno-114-6" href="#__codelineno-114-6"></a><span class="cp">#DATA</span>
<a id="__codelineno-114-7" name="__codelineno-114-7" href="#__codelineno-114-7"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// b=250</span>
<a id="__codelineno-114-8" name="__codelineno-114-8" href="#__codelineno-114-8"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">byte</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Muppets</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"d=4,o=5,b=15,"</span><span class="p">,</span>

<h3 id="tune_pause">tune_Pause</h3>
<p>Suspends any current tune from playing until a <a href="#tune_continue"><strong>tune_Continue()</strong></a>, <a href="#tune_stop"><strong>tune_Stop()</strong></a> or a new <a href="#tune_play"><strong>tune_Play("...")</strong></a> function is called. The oscillator is not stopped.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>tune_Pause();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#tune_play">tune_Play(..)</a></p>
<h3 id="tune_continue">tune_Continue</h3>
<p>Continues playing any previously stopped or paused tune.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>tune_Continue();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#tune_play">tune_Play(..)</a></p>
<h3 id="tune_stop">tune_Stop</h3>
<p>Pauses a tune and silences the oscillator until a <a href="#tune_continue"><strong>tune_Continue()</strong></a>, <a href="#tune_stop"><strong>tune_Stop()</strong></a>, <a href="#tune_stop"><strong>tune_End()</strong></a> or a new <a href="#tune_play"><strong>tune_Play("...")</strong></a> function is called.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>tune_Stop();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#tune_play">tune_Play(..)</a></p>
<h3 id="tune_end">tune_End</h3>
<p>Ends any current tune and resets the tune interpreter.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>tune_End();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#tune_play">tune_Play(..)</a></p>
<h3 id="tune_playing">tune_Playing</h3>
<p>Use this function to check for any current tunes being played. Returns 1 if tune is playing, 0 if no tune is playing.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>tune_Playing();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if a tune is playing Returns: 0 if no tune is playing    |</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#tune_play">tune_Play(..)</a></p>
<h3 id="beep">beep</h3>
<p>Simple utility to produce a single musical note for the required duration.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>beep(note, duration);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">note</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the frequency of the note. Note could be between 0 and 64</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">duration</td>

</tr>

</table></div></div>

<h2 class="page-break" id="general-purpose-functions">General Purpose Functions</h2>
<h3 id="lookup8">lookup8</h3>
<p>Search a list of 8-bit constant values for a match with a search value <strong>key</strong>. If found, the index of the matching constant is returned in <strong>result</strong>, else <strong>result</strong> is set to <strong>0</strong>. Thus, if the value is found first in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to <strong>1</strong>. If second in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to <strong>2</strong> etc. If not found, <strong>result</strong> is returned with <strong>0</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>lookup8(key, byteConstList);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">key</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A byte value to search for in a fixed list of constants. The <strong>key</strong> argument can be a variable, array element, expression or constant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">byteConsList</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A comma separated list of constants and strings to be matched against <strong>key</strong>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: Index/Position of the matching constant starting with 1. 0 if 'key' doesn't exist</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-116-1" name="__codelineno-116-1" href="#__codelineno-116-1"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<a id="__codelineno-116-2" name="__codelineno-116-2" href="#__codelineno-116-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">key</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">r</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-116-3" name="__codelineno-116-3" href="#__codelineno-116-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-116-4" name="__codelineno-116-4" href="#__codelineno-116-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">key</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'a'</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-116-5" name="__codelineno-116-5" href="#__codelineno-116-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">lookup8</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">key</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x4D</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"abcd"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'Z'</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>The list of constants cannot be re-directed.</li>
<li>This offers a versatile way for returning an index for a given value. This can be very useful for data entry filtering and parameter input checking and wherever you need to check the validity of certain inputs.</li>
<li>The entire search list field can be replaced with a single name if you use the $ operator in constant, eg: <code>#constant HEXVALUES $"0123456789ABCDEF"</code></li>
</ul>
</div>
<h3 id="lookup16">lookup16</h3>
<p>Search a list of 16-bit constant values for a match with a search value <strong>key</strong>. If found, the index of the matching constant is returned in <strong>result</strong>, else <strong>result</strong> is set to <strong>0</strong>. Thus, if the value is found first in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to <strong>1</strong>. If second in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to <strong>2</strong> etc. If not found, <strong>result</strong> is returned with <strong>0</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>lookup16(key, wordConstList);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">key</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A word value to search for in a fixed list of constants. The <strong>key</strong> argument can be a variable, array element, expression or constant</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">wordConstList</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A comma separated list of constants to be matched against <strong>key</strong>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: Index/Position of the matching constant starting with 1. 0 if 'key' doesn't exist</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-117-1" name="__codelineno-117-1" href="#__codelineno-117-1"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<a id="__codelineno-117-2" name="__codelineno-117-2" href="#__codelineno-117-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">key</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">r</span><span class="p">;</span>

<a id="__codelineno-117-9" name="__codelineno-117-9" href="#__codelineno-117-9"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">Search value 5000 </span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">found at index "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">r</span><span class="p">);</span>

</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This offers a versatile way for returning an index for a given value. This can be very useful for data entry filtering and parameter input checking and wherever you need to check the validity of certain inputs.</li>

<h3 class="page-break" id="pause">pause</h3>
<p>Stop execution of the user program for a predetermined amount of time.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>pause(time);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">time</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value specifying the delay time in milliseconds.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-118-1" name="__codelineno-118-1" href="#__codelineno-118-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">joystick</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">==</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">FIRE</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// if fire button pressed</span>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li><em>SYSTEM</em> registers are maintained by internal system functions and should not be written to. They should only ever be read. <strong>DO NOT</strong> write to these registers.</li>
<li><em>USER</em> registers are read/write (R/W) registers used to alter the system behaviour. Refer to the individual functions for information on the interaction with these registers.</li>
<li>These registers are accessible with <a href="#peekb">peekB</a> and <a href="#pokeb">pokeB</a> functions.</li>
<li>Regiter Addresses 162-165 (or 0xA2 to 0xA5) are <strong>RESERVED</strong> 8-bit Registers</li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li><em>SYSTEM</em> registers are maintained by internal system functions and should not be written to. They should only ever be read. <strong>DO NOT</strong> write to these registers.</li>
<li><em>USER</em> registers are read/write (R/W) registers used to alter the system behaviour. Refer to the individual functions for information on the interaction with these registers.</li>
<li><em>USERSTACK</em> are used by the debugging and system extension utilities</li>
<li><em>MEMORY</em> - 255-word size variables for users program</li>
<li><em>STACK</em> - 128 word EVE system stack (STACK grows upwards)s</li>
<li><em>FLAGS</em> are a mixture of bits that are either maintained by internal system functions or set/cleared by various system functions. Refer to the <a href="#flags_bit_map">Flags Register Bit Map tables</a>, and individual functions for further details.</li>
<li>These registers are accessible with <a href="#peekw">peekW</a> and <a href="#pokew">pokeW</a> functions.</li>
</ul>
</div>

<td style="text-align: center;">_OW_PIN</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 = IO1, 1 = IO2 (Dallas OW Pin)</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0010</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 5</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_PTR_TYPE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Used internally</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0020</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 6</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_TEMP1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Used internally</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0040</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 7</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_TEMP2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Used internally</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0080</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 8</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_RUNMODE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 = running pcode from media</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0100</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 9</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_SIGNED</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 = number printed '-' prepend</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0200</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 10</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_RUNFLAG</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 = EVE processor is running</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0400</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 11</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_SINGLESTEP</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 = set breakpoint for debugger</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0800</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 12</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_COMMINT</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 = buffered coms active</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x1000</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 13</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_DUMMY16</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 = display needs 16bit dummy</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x2000</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 14</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_DISP16</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 = display is 16bit interface</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x4000</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bit 15</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">_PROPFONT</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 = current font is proportional</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x8000</td>
</tr>

<h2 class="page-break" id="hardware-tools">Hardware Tools</h2>
<p>The following hardware tools are required for full control of the GOLDELOX Processor.</p>
<h3 id="programming-tools">Programming Tools</h3>
<p>The 4D Programming Cable, uUSB-PA5-II and 4D-UPA Programming Adaptors are essential hardware tools to program, customise and test the GOLDELOX Processor. </p>
<p>The 4D programming interfaces are used to program a new Firmware/PmmC, Display Driver and for downloading compiled 4DGL code into the processor. They even serve as an interface for communicating serial data to the PC.</p>
<p>The 4D Programming Cable, uUSB-PA5 and gen4-PA Programming Adaptor are available from <a href="https://4dsystems.com.au">4D Systems</a>.</p>
<p>Using a non-4D programming interface could damage your processor and <strong><u>void your Warranty</u></strong>.</p>
<div class="flex-column align-bottom">
<figure class="flex-1">
<p><img alt="4D Programming Cable" class="width-80" src="../img/goldelox/image5.png"></p>
<figcaption>4D Programming Cable</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure class="flex-1">
<p><img alt="uUSB-PA5-II" class="width-60" src="../img/goldelox/image6.png"></p>
<figcaption>uUSB-PA5-II</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure class="flex-1">
<p><img alt="4D-UPA" class="width-40" src="../img/goldelox/image7.png"></p>
<figcaption>4D-UPA</figcaption>
</figure>
</div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Any of the 4D Programming Cable, uUSB-PA5-II or 4D-UPA Programming Adaptor can be used, along with previous generation 4D programmers too.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="display-modules">Display Modules</h3>
<p>The following modules, available from 4D Systems, can be used for evaluation purposes to discover what the GOLDELOX processor has to offer.</p>
<figure>
<p><img alt="uOLED-128-G2" class="width-60" src="../img/goldelox/image8.png"></p>
<figcaption>uOLED-128-G2</figcaption>
</figure>
<p>Other modules, such as the 0.96” and 1.7” OLED, or 1.44” LCD versions are also available. Please contact 4D Systems for more information, or visit the <a href="https://4dsystems.com.au">4D Systems website</a>.</p>
<h2 class="page-break" id="software-tools">Software Tools</h2>
<p>Workshop4 is a comprehensive software IDE that provides an integrated software development platform for all the 4D family of processors and modules.
The IDE combines the Editor, Compiler, Linker and Down- Loader to develop complete 4DGL application code.
All user application code is developed within the Workshop4 IDE.</p>
<p><img alt="WS4 Recent Page" src="../img/goldelox/image10.png"></p>
<p>The Workshop4 IDE supports multiple development environments for the user, to cater for different user requirements and skill level.</p>
<ul>
<li>The <strong>Designer</strong> environment enables the user to write 4DGL code in its natural form to program the GOLDELOX module. </li>
<li>A visual programming experience, suitably called <strong>ViSi</strong>, enables drag-and-drop type placement of objects to assist with 4DGL code generation and allows the user to visualise how the display will look while being developed. </li>
<li>A <strong>Serial</strong> environment is also provided to transform the GOLDELOX module into a slave serial module, allowing the user to control the display from any host microcontroller or device with a serial port.</li>
</ul>
<p>For a comprehensive manual on the Workshop4 IDE Software along with other documents, refer to the <a href="../../workshop4/">Workshop4 User Manual</a>.</p>
